text: DSH Work Diary 是面向 DSH Web 的每日工作日记插件，在侧栏提供日记面板。它按日期收集活跃会话，将会话请求与结论整理成摘要交给模型，并流式生成 Markdown 日记；支持选择日期、查看会话、手动重新生成及每日定时运行，也可设置总结模型、语言和详略程度。适合希望回顾当天 DSH 工作的人。

DSH Work Diary adds a diary panel to the DSH Web sidebar. It collects sessions for a chosen date and streams a Markdown work summary from the configured model. Choose a date, inspect sessions, regenerate the summary, or enable a daily schedule. Model, language, and detail level are configurable.
想把 DSH 今天做过的工作整理成一篇日记。
Can DSH turn my sessions from a selected day into a work summary?
DSH Work Diary 的功能「按日生成工作日记」：从侧栏日记面板选择日期并点击生成，插件收集当天活跃会话的请求和结论，交给选定模型流式生成 Markdown 总结。
DSH Work Diary 使用所选模型生成总结时，会把当天会话整理出的摘要文本发送给 DSH 的 llm 服务；具体模型和服务由配置决定。

@smwyylc/dsh-work-diary README · dsh-work-diary：English | [中文](README.zh.md)

A daily work diary for the DSH Web GUI. The sidebar gains a "Diary" icon; opening it gathers the sessions that had activity on a given day and turns them into one Markdown diary entry. It can run on a schedule every day or on demand, and the model used for the summary is configurable.

@smwyylc/dsh-work-diary README · dsh-work-diary：A dozen sessions and a few dozen tool calls in one day, and by the evening you rarely remember what you actually did. This plugin flips through those sessions for you and saves them into a readable diary — you do not read the whole thing, it only has to say roughly "what got done today". The default tier costs about 8900-11600 tokens once a day.

@smwyylc/dsh-work-diary README · What it does：- Picks the sessions that had activity on one day in local time (today by default, switchable to yesterday or any date). "Active" is judged by the last real human question, so a long session that keeps running across days is not missed.
- Each session contributes only metadata, its first user request, and its last assistant conclusion, plus the file names its tool calls touched, assembled into a digest handed to the model. The last assistant conclusion answers "what finally got done", which is more direct than the first request — the request says what you wanted; when the last line is only half a sentence it falls back to the previous complete conclusion and is marked "(in progress)".
- The model writes fixed sections: today's overview / the work done today listed by project; the complete tier adds one more section for leftovers and the next step.
- The panel always lists that day's sessions below; clicking a card jumps straight to that session.

@smwyylc/dsh-work-diary README · Install：From npm, or from any plugin market that indexes it:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add @smwyylc/dsh-work-diary
```

Or install a checkout as a local bundle: `lib/index.js` is the Host half, `lib/client.js` is the Client half, `cordis.patch.yml` declares the row to mount, and `icon.svg` is the sidebar icon; there is no build step.

@smwyylc/dsh-work-diary README · Install：1. Put this directory anywhere (next to your other plugins is fine).
2. Use the DSH plugin manager's "Install local bundle" to install it into the current profile. This step writes the profile's dependency and mount for you; no hand-editing of the profile.
3. Restart DSH and a "Diary" icon appears in the sidebar.

After changing the code a restart is required: modules are loaded at process start.

@smwyylc/dsh-work-diary README · Usage：For a date that already has a summary the button reads "Regenerate" — every click is a real model call.
When the model output hits the length cap it is marked below the body, and that run's ending may be half a sentence.

@smwyylc/dsh-work-diary README · Expected cost：Basis: **input = that day's digests of every session + the fixed template** (267 characters for the brief template, 299 for the complete one). Reading sessions and scanning file names out of tool calls are local disk I/O and cost no tokens; only the generation call hits the model. The table below samples a day of 13 sessions; doubling the session count roughly doubles the input and leaves the output unchanged.

@smwyylc/dsh-work-diary README · Expected cost：| Item | Brief (default) | Complete |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Input characters (digest + fixed template) | about 10-12k | about 13-17k |
| Input tokens (at 1.5 characters/token) | about 6700-8000 | about 8700-11300 |
| Output + thinking tokens | about 2200-3600 | about 2600-4000 |
| Total tokens for the day | about 8900-11600 | about 11300-15300 |

@smwyylc/dsh-work-diary README · Expected cost：The input half comes from the conclusion budget being raised from 500 to 1000 characters (which pushed the brief tier's input from about 4400 tokens to about 6.7k) and from the "backfill the previous complete conclusion when the last line is too short" rule (see the next section). How much a backfill recovers depends on the session itself — measured on the same day, a backfill may add only 45 characters or recover 900, which is why the input bounds are far apart. Usually only one or two of the 13 sessions trigger it.

@smwyylc/dsh-work-diary README · Expected cost：The output half is dominated by thinking, which the gateway will not let anyone switch off (see "How it saves token"). On 2026-10-28 the brief tier measured 2920 input tokens plus 2710 output tokens on a six-session day, and the complete tier 4185 plus 3067. Doubling the session count roughly doubles the input and leaves the output unchanged.

@smwyylc/dsh-work-diary README · Expected cost：It runs automatically once a day. With "Generate daily on a schedule" turned off the fixed cost is 0 and a call only happens when you click "Generate summary".

@smwyylc/dsh-work-diary README · How it saves tokens：The default tier compresses layer by layer, from sampling to output, keeping only what is needed to answer "what got done today".

**Sampling**: each session sends two lines of body (first request + last conclusion), and the session header names a few files.

@smwyylc/dsh-work-diary README · How it saves tokens：- The request carries a hard `maxTokens` cap (4000 brief / 6000 complete). The cap has to cover **thinking plus body** together: on 2026-10-28 every one of eight tested models returned an empty body at 900 tokens, because their thinking runs 1500-9000 characters and eats the whole budget before any body appears. Word limits stay in the prompt (600 characters for brief, 800 for complete); measured at the 4000 cap two models wrote 724 and 741 characters, so they mostly obey.
- Thinking cannot be switched off through this gateway. Six spellings were tried on 2026-10-28 (`reasoning_effort=none/low/minimal`, `enable_thinking=false`, `thinking.type=disabled`, and sending nothing): the gateway accepts them all without error and forwards none of them, so thinking never drops below roughly 460 characters, and `reasoning_effort=none` on a real digest sometimes made it longer (6536 characters). The only lever left is the prompt, which now explicitly forbids thinking, analysis and draft output; in a controlled run that took the body from empty to 905 characters. Thinking is therefore the larger half of the output cost and the main reason the
@smwyylc/dsh-work-diary README · Configuration：Settings are saved in `[DSH_HOME]/work-diary/settings.json` (`~/.dsh` when `DSH_HOME` is unset). Fields:

@smwyylc/dsh-work-diary README · Configuration：| Field | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | `true` | Whether to generate automatically on a schedule every day |
| `time` | `18:00` | Local time HH:MM, runs once when the time arrives |
| `provider` | empty | Provider of the summary model; empty provider and model means follow the default model |
| `model` | empty | Model of the summary model |
| `language` | `zh` | Output language, `zh` or `en` |
| `verbosity` | `brief` | Detail level: `brief` (token-saving) / `full` |
| `maxSessions` | `40` | Maximum sessions included in one summary; the panel reports the count beyond it |

@smwyylc/dsh-work-diary README · Configuration：The settings panel can change the switch, the time, provider / model, language and detail level; `maxSessions` needs a hand edit of `settings.json` and takes effect on the next start.

Automatic execution: one run for the current day when the time arrives (the panel status shows "auto"). If the day has no result yet at DSH startup and the set time has passed, a catch-up run fires immediately; the word `catch-up` appears in the Host log.

@smwyylc/dsh-work-diary README · Configuration：Generated results are saved by date in `[DSH_HOME]/work-diary/last-runs.json`, keeping the latest 30. Opening the panel for a date that already has a result shows it directly without generating again.

@smwyylc/dsh-work-diary README · Where the data comes from：- The session list is the union of two paths: sessions whose `updatedAt` in `sessionController.list()` (the last real human question, taken from the persisted projection cache) falls on that day, plus sessions created in the last 7 days. The projection cache is not full coverage, so sessions it misses fall back to `updatedAt` = creation time and get dropped; the second path patches that hole, and `readSession`'s real event times give the final verdict. The second path is append-only: guessing wrong only reads a few extra sessions and never misses one.
- Each session is read exactly once through `sessionQuery.readSession`: header, title, counts, all real human requests, the last assistant conclusion and tool-call events in one go. listEvents / readEvent / readSession each load the full session log every time and the observation cache holds only 5 LRU entries, so one extra read multiplies the wait.
- Requests count only real human input: `source.kind === 'user'` on `user/message` counts, agent-injected context does not; a session with no real human input is skipped entirely.
- The conclusion takes `assistant/message`'s `data.
